name: _validate_sparse_csc_tensor_args
description: Representative ATen signature (not an exclusive ABI), copied verbatim: aten::_validate_sparse_csc_tensor_args(Tensor ccol_indices, Tensor row_indices, Tensor values, int[] size) -> (). Registered schemas supplied for this operator: aten::_validate_sparse_csc_tensor_args(Tensor ccol_indices, Tensor row_indices, Tensor values, int[] size) -> (). This is the only registered overload (the native operator probes as overloads() == ["default"]), so no .out or alternate-signature form exists; the representative signature is nevertheless not exclusive. The original Gems pytest owns the full contract and defines the overloads, keyword arguments, returns, errors, aliasing and mutation it supports; do not narrow, delete or rewrite those tests to fit this single signature. Semantics: host-side and device-side validation of the arguments of a CSC (compressed sparse column) tensor. The worker checks host preconditions on the three operands and the size list - size rank must match batch + 2 + dense_ndim, ccol_indices must have rank batch_ndim + 1 (so a non-batched structure passes a 1-D ccol_indices of length ncols + 1, and a 0-dim ccol_indices is rejected), row_indices must have rank batch_ndim + 1 and values must have rank batch_ndim + 1 + dense_ndim, with row_indices and values sharing the leading batch dimensions, ccol_indices must have last dimension ncols + 1, row_indices and values must share the stored-entry count nnz, ccol_indices and row_indices last dimensions must be dense per batch (stride 1), index dtypes must be int32 or int64, both index tensors must share one index dtype, index dtypes must be able to represent ncols + 1, nnz + 1 and nrows, and the meta path applies only when all three tensors are on the meta device and there are no stored entries. On the device a kernel additionally checks that column entries are sorted and distinct, that ccol_indices[..., -1] == nnz, that ccol_indices[..., 0] >= 0 and that stored column slices are contiguous per batch. The operator returns nothing (void) and must not modify the tensors it inspects; a valid call is observable only through acceptance of the call, a None return and untouched operands and view geometry. Invalid schemas (missing size, non-tensor ccol_indices, non-int-list size, float entry in size) and host precondition or index-dtype violations raise RuntimeError or TypeError; the malformed index-content cases abort under CUDA_KERNEL_ASSERT instead of raising and remain an unresolved part of the native contract.
